plan: Given my value of $3, I should bid below this value to avoid a loss. Since all bidders are rational and aim to maximize profit, they will not bid above their value. I will bid slightly above half my value to potentially win if others undervalue or bid conservatively. Thus, I choose to bid $1.5.

Given my value of $24, I aim to bid slightly below my value to maximize potential profit while ensuring a competitive bid. A rational bidder knows bidding above their value is illogical due to potential losses. I will bid just under my value to potentially win without overpaying, considering others will also bid rationally. I will bid $23.9, maximizing my chance of winning while ensuring profit if I do win. This strategy accounts for the rational nature of all bidders.

My value for the prize is $11. To maximize profit, I should bid slightly above the expected third-highest bid, which is the average value, $24.5, minus some margin. However, since my value is $11, I should bid lower to avoid overpaying. A bid of $10.9 ensures I only win if others bid very low, minimizing loss if I win.
